items.stem: A block slides down a rough plane inclined at 45° to the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.4. Find its acceleration. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: Along the plane: mg sin θ − μₖmg cos θ = ma ⇒ a = g(sin θ − μₖ cos θ) = 9.8(0.707 − 0.4 × 0.707) = 4.16 m s⁻².

items.stem: Find the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Moon (mass 1/81 and radius 0.27 of the Earth's). (g on Earth = 9.8 m s⁻²)
For A = 2î − 1ĵ + 0k̂ and B = 2î + 0ĵ + 4k̂, find A × B, its magnitude, and hence the area of the parallelogram formed by A and B.
items.answer: A × B = −4î − 8ĵ + 2k̂; |A × B| = 9.17; area = 9.17 square units
items.markingKey: Expand the determinant (2): A × B = −4î − 8ĵ + 2k̂; magnitude √(16 + 64 + 4) = 9.17 (1); area of parallelogram = |A × B| (1).

items.stem: Rock at the base of a mountain begins to flow when the stress exceeds about 3 × 10⁸ N m⁻². If the density of rock is 3000 kg m⁻³, estimate the maximum height of a mountain on Earth. Why could mountains on Mars (g ≈ 3.7 m s⁻²) be taller? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.answer: About 10 km; on Mars smaller g means a taller column for the same stress
items.markingKey: Stress at base = hρg (1); hρg ≤ σ ⇒ h = σ/(ρg) = 3 × 10⁸/(3000 × 9.8) = 10200 m ≈ 10 km (1); h ∝ 1/g, so mountains on Mars can be about 2.6 times taller (Olympus Mons ≈ 22 km) (1).

items.stem: A fielder throws a ball at 50 m s⁻¹. At what angles to the horizontal can it be thrown to land 229.6 m away on level ground? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)

In a resonance-column experiment, Varun uses a tuning fork of 384 Hz and finds the first two resonance lengths of the air column as 20.9 cm and 64.6 cm. Find the speed of sound in air and the end correction.
items.markingKey: l₂ − l₁ = λ/2 ⇒ λ = 2(64.6 − 20.9) cm = 87.5 cm (1); v = νλ = 336 m s⁻¹ (1); end correction e = (l₂ − 3l₁)/2 = 1.0 cm (1).

items.stem:
Sahil reads that a power-plant steam engine takes in steam at 327 °C and condenses it at 27 °C. In each cycle it absorbs 10000 J. Its actual efficiency is 25%.
(i) Find the Carnot (maximum) efficiency. (ii) Find the work done per cycle. (iii) Find the heat rejected per cycle. (iv) Why is the actual efficiency less than the Carnot value?
items.answer: (i) 50.0% (ii) 2500 J (iii) 7500 J (iv) real engines are irreversible: friction, heat losses
items.markingKey: (i) 1 − T₂/T₁ (1). (ii) ηQ₁ (1). (iii) Q₁ − W (1). (iv) irreversibility (1).

items.stem:
At a small hydroelectric plant in Himachal Pradesh, water falls through a height of 20 m and 500 kg of water passes through the turbine every second. Lakshmi learns that the plant converts 70% of the water's potential energy into electrical energy. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
(i) Find the potential energy lost by the water per second. (ii) Find the electrical power output. (iii) Find the speed of the water just before reaching the turbine (no losses). (iv) Name one form into which the remaining energy is converted.
items.answer: (i) 98000 J (ii) 68.6 kW (iii) 19.8 m s⁻¹ (iv) heat/sound (internal energy)
items.markingKey: (i) mgh per second = 98000 J (1). (ii) 70% of it = 68600 W (1). (iii) √(2gh) (1). (iv) heat, sound or friction losses (1).

items.stem: A hole of diameter 4.24 cm is drilled in a copper sheet at 27 °C. What is its diameter when the sheet is heated to 127 °C? Explain why the hole becomes larger, not smaller. (α_copper = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)
items.markingKey: The hole expands like the material that would fill it (1). Δd = αdΔT = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ × 4.24 × 100 = 0.00721 cm (1); new diameter 4.2472 cm (1).

items.stem: Aarav walks from home to a market 1.5 km away at 5 km h⁻¹. Finding it closed, Aarav turns back at once and walks home at 7.5 km h⁻¹. Find the magnitude of average velocity and the average speed over the interval 0 to 25 min.
items.answer: Average velocity 1.50 km h⁻¹; average speed 5.70 km h⁻¹
items.markingKey: Outward time 18 min. In the remaining 7 min the return distance is 7.5 × 0.1167 = 0.875 km. Displacement 0.625 km, path 2.375 km in 25 min = 0.4167 h; |v_av| = 1.50 km h⁻¹, speed = 5.70 km h⁻¹.

items.stem: A particle in SHM has speeds 24.7 cm s⁻¹ and 24.0 cm s⁻¹ when its displacements are 4 cm and 5 cm. Find the amplitude and the period.

items.stem:
Ishaan reads that the viscous force on a small ball falling through honey is F = 6πηrv, where r is the radius, v the speed and η the coefficient of viscosity. The value of η for honey is 10 Pa s.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): On a banked road no friction is needed at any speed.
Reason (R): At the optimum speed the normal reaction alone provides the centripetal force.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false (only at the optimum speed); R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:

Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Doubling the absolute temperature of a gas doubles the r.m.s. speed of its molecules.
Reason (R): v_rms ∝ √T.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false (it becomes √2 times); R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A boat can move at 3 m s⁻¹ in still water. It heads perpendicular to the bank of a river 300 m wide flowing at 1 m s⁻¹. Find the time to cross and how far downstream it lands.
items.markingKey: t = width/v_b = 300/3 = 100 s; drift = v_r t = 1 × 100 = 100 m.

items.stem: A metre stick is balanced on a knife edge at its centre (the 50 cm mark). A 25 g mass hangs at the 30 cm mark. Where must a 40 g mass be hung to balance the stick?
The breaking stress of copper is about 2.2 × 10⁸ N m⁻². What is the largest mass that can be hung from a copper wire of diameter 2 mm without breaking it? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
A pendulum bob on a string 0.5 m long is pulled aside until the string makes 45° with the vertical, and released. Find its speed at the lowest point. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: Height fall h = L(1 − cos θ) = 0.1464 m; v = √(2gh) = 1.69 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular sheet are 74.57 m and 8.46 m. Find its area to the correct number of significant figures.
items.markingKey: 74.57 × 8.46 = 630.862 m²; the product keeps the least number of significant figures in the data (three, from 8.46 m), so 631 m².

items.stem: How much work is done in blowing a soap bubble of radius 3 cm? (Surface tension of soap solution = 0.025 N m⁻¹)
items.markingKey: Two surfaces: W = S × 2 × 4πr² = 8πr²S = 5.65 × 10⁻⁴ J.

items.stem: A body starts with velocity 4 m s⁻¹ and moves with uniform acceleration 6 m s⁻². How far does it travel during the 6th second?

Tara heats a 200 g metal block to 150 °C and drops it into 200 g of water at 25 °C in an insulated vessel (neglect its heat capacity). The final temperature is 35.6 °C. Find the specific heat capacity of the metal. (c_water = 4186 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹)
items.markingKey: Heat lost by metal = mc(150 − 35.6); heat gained by water = 0.2 × 4186 × (35.6 − 25) = 8870 J (2); c = 388 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: Two identical waves of amplitude 5 mm and wavelength 0.8 m travel in opposite directions on a string with a node at x = 0. Find the amplitude of vibration at x = 0.1 m.
items.markingKey: y = 2A sin(kx) cos ωt (1); amplitude = 2A|sin(2πx/λ)| = 10 × |sin(45°)| (1) = 7.07 mm (1).

items.stem: A shell of mass 25 g is fired horizontally from a gun of mass 2 kg with a muzzle speed of 300 m s⁻¹. Find the recoil speed of the gun. If the gun is stopped by the shoulder in 0.2 s, what is the average force on the shoulder?
A particle executes SHM of amplitude 8 cm and period 3.14 s. Find its maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
items.markingKey: ω = 2π/T = 2.00 rad s⁻¹; v_max = Aω = 0.160 m s⁻¹; a_max = Aω² = 0.320 m s⁻².

items.stem: A Carnot engine with its sink at 17 °C has an efficiency of 25%. By how many degrees must the source temperature be raised to increase the efficiency to 50%?

At a district athletics meet, Vihaan takes off for a long jump at 10 m s⁻¹ at 35° to the horizontal. Treat Vihaan as a projectile (g = 9.8 m s⁻²).
(i) Find the horizontal component of take-off velocity. (ii) Find the time in the air. (iii) Find the length of the jump. (iv) What would the jump be at the same speed if the take-off angle were 45°?
items.markingKey: (i) u cos θ (1). (ii) 2u sin θ/g (1). (iii) u² sin 2θ/g = 9.59 m (1). (iv) u²/g = 10.2 m (1).

items.stem:
Siddharth spins a potter's wheel (a uniform disc of mass 1.5 kg and radius 25 cm) up to 10 rad s⁻¹ and lets it go. Friction brings it to rest uniformly in 10 s.
(i) Find the moment of inertia. (ii) Find the angular deceleration. (iii) Find the frictional torque. (iv) Find the number of revolutions before it stops.
items.markingKey: (i) ½MR² (1). (ii) α = ω/t (1). (iii) τ = Iα (1). (iv) θ = ½ωt = 50.0 rad ÷ 2π (1).

items.stem: A steel wire of length 1 m and a copper wire of length 1 m, both of diameter 1 mm, are joined end to end. The combination is loaded with 14 kg. Find the extension of each wire. (Y_steel = 2.0 × 10¹¹ N m⁻², Y_copper = 1.1 × 10¹¹ N m⁻², g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: Same tension 137.2 N in both (1); A = 7.85 × 10⁻⁷ m² (0.5); ΔL = FL/(AY): steel 8.73 × 10⁻⁴ m, copper 0.00159 m (1.5).

items.stem: Derive expressions for the final velocities of two bodies in a one-dimensional elastic collision, the second initially at rest.
items.markingKey: Momentum equation (1); KE equation (1); combine to get u₁ + v₁ = v₂ (1); solve (2).

items.stem: The density of aluminium is 2.7 g cm⁻³. (i) Express it in SI units. (ii) Find the mass of 400 cm³ of aluminium in kilogram, to three significant figures.
items.markingKey: (i) 1 g cm⁻³ = 10⁻³ kg / 10⁻⁶ m³ = 10³ kg m⁻³, so 2700 kg m⁻³ (1 mark). (ii) m = ρV = 2.7 × 400 = 1080 g = 1.08 kg (2 marks).
